Kerberos for Single Sign-On
Kerberos for single sign-on (SSO) is a idx_c3859d4b secure authentication protocol idx_59b6b900 that allows users to
access multiple resources without repeatedly idx_9362b1bf entering their credentials. When integrated with
Microsoft Entra Private Access, Kerberos SSO streamlines access to on-premises applications
and resources by using users' existing Active Directory credentials. This means that once a user
signs in and is authenticated, a Kerberos ticket is issued, which can then be used to
transparently access other resources within the organization's network that support Kerberos
authentication.
With Microsoft Entra Private Access, organizations can enable Kerberos SSO for applications
that are not directly exposed to the internet but require secure, seamless authentication. This

Source IP anchoring
Source IP anchoring is a network-security technique that ensures your outbound traffic always
appears to idx_c293f4dc come from a specific, predictable public IP address, even when users are remote,
mobile, or connecting through distributed cloud edges. This matters because idx_6024694b many SaaS and
line-of-business apps still rely on IP allowlists or location-based access controls to decide who
can connect.
It forces selected traffic to egress through a fixed IP controlled by your organization. Even if a
user is working from home, roaming, or connecting through a cloud security service, the
application sees the same trusted IP.
This is used to:
Maintain compatibility with legacy SaaS apps that require static IP allowlisting.
Enforce network-based access policies without forcing all traffic through a physical
office.
Support Zero Trust transitions while keeping older controls intact.
Microsoft Entra Private Access routes specific application traffic through a private network
connector, so the app always sees an organization-owned egress IP. This satisfies apps that
enforce access based on known network locations. This is done by configuring an enterprise
application in GSA. The GSA client on the device then acquires the traffic and routes it through
the GSA service to a private network with a private network connector configured. The private
network connector then passes the traffic through the egress point to the SaaS application. The
following figure shows the traffic flow.
Figure 15.11: Source IP anchoring
In the above example, the SaaS application only accepts traffic from a predefined IP address
which is the egress point of the organization's on-premises network. GSA routes traffic from all
clients through the SSE tunnel where Conditional Access policies can be applied. The traffic is
then sent to the on-premises network using the Private Network Connector and uses the egress
point to connect to the SaaS application. The SaaS application recognizes the IP address and
allows access.

Private Access for Domain Controllers
Ensuring private access for domain controllers is critical for safeguarding sensitive
authentication idx_a4250bb0 and directory services within an organization. Exposing domain controllers to
the public internet poses significant security risks, including unauthorized access and
potential data breaches. Microsoft Entra Private Access provides a secure, identity-centric
solution that enables users to connect to domain controllers from any device or network
without exposing them to external threats. By leveraging Microsoft Entra Private Access,
organizations can maintain strict control over who can access on-premises applications that
use Kerberos authentication by enforcing Conditional Access policies and ensuring that only
authenticated and authorized users are granted entry, significantly reducing the attack surface.

Application usage analytics
Application usage analytics in GSA provide critical insights into how users are engaging with
both on-premises idx_0ae3199b and cloud-based applications within your organization. By leveraging these
analytics, administrators can monitor user access patterns, identify frequently accessed
applications, and detect anomalies or potential security risks. The analytics dashboard
typically presents data such as the number of unique users per application, session durations,
peak usage times, and trends in application adoption over time.
These insights help IT teams make informed decisions about resource allocation, policy
adjustments, and access controls. For example, applications that show unusually high or
unexpected access patterns can be investigated for potential misuse or security concerns.
Conversely, underutilized applications can be reviewed for relevance or decommissioning.
Application usage analytics also support compliance initiatives by providing an auditable trail
of who accessed what applications, when, and from where.
In the context of Global Secure Access, usage analytics are further enhanced by integrating
with identity-centric controls. This ensures that visibility extends across hybrid environments,
supporting Zero Trust principles. Ultimately, robust analytics empower organizations to
optimize application portfolios, improve user productivity, and strengthen overall security
posture.
The dashboard is available in the Microsoft Entra Admin center by navigating to Global Secure

Logs and idx_fa43efc9 monitoring form the operational backbone of GSA. They provide the visibility needed
to understand how traffic flows through the network, how policies are being applied, and
where risks or performance issues may be emerging. Because GSA sits at the intersection of
identity, network access, and Zero Trust enforcement, its logging model brings together signals

GSA Dashboard
The Global Secure Access dashboard provides a consolidated, real-time view of how identity-
aware idx_209b1b57 network access is performing across the environment. It surfaces key metrics such as
connector health, session volumes, policy outcomes, and traffic patterns, allowing teams to
quickly spot anomalies or degradation. Visual summaries highlight trends in access requests,
blocked sessions, device posture, and user experience signals. Because the dashboard unifies
identity, network, and device telemetry, it becomes a central command surface for monitoring
Zero Trust enforcement. It also links directly to deeper analytics and logs, helping
administrators move from high-level insights to detailed investigation with minimal friction.
The GSA Dashboard is accessible in the Microsoft Entra Admin center by navigating to Global
Secure Access | Dashboard.
Traffic logs
Traffic logs in Global Secure Access provide detailed visibility into how users, devices, and
applications idx_0551a197 interact across the identity-aware network fabric. They capture information such
as source and destination, protocols used, session duration, data volume, and policy outcomes.
This telemetry helps administrators understand access patterns, validate segmentation, and
troubleshoot performance or connectivity issues. Traffic logs also reveal anomalies like
unexpected destinations or unusual data transfers, supporting threat detection, and forensic
investigations. Because they correlate identity, device posture, and network behavior, traffic
logs become a critical component of Zero Trust monitoring, enabling continuous verification,
and informed policy refinement.
Traffic logs are retained in the system for 30 days. To view these logs, administrators must have
the Global Secure Access Administrator or the Global Secure Access Log Reader role.

Audit logs in Global Secure Access capture the administrative actions that shape how the
service operates, providing a traceable record of configuration changes, policy updates,
connector idx_a5af64ff management, and role assignments. These logs help establish accountability by
showing who performed an action, when it occurred, and what settings were modified.
Because GSA spans identity, network access, and device posture, audit logs become essential
for compliance and operational governance. They support investigations by linking
administrative activity to downstream effects such as policy enforcement outcomes or traffic
shifts. Consistent review of audit logs strengthens change control and ensures the access fabric

provisioned, updated, and expanded across an environment. They capture events such as

configuration propagation to remote networks. These logs help administrators verify that new
components have been deployed correctly, identify failures during rollout, and ensure that
changes have reached all required endpoints. Because GSA relies on distributed connectors and
cloud-managed policies, deployment logs become essential for validating consistency,
troubleshooting onboarding issues, and maintaining a predictable, well-governed access
fabric.
To view these logs, administrators must have the Global Secure Access Administrator or the

Types of threats facing Microsoft Entra
The threat landscape for identity and access management platforms is dynamic and complex.
Microsoft idx_549074b1 Entra, as a central authentication authority, is a high-value target for attackers
seeking to compromise organizational security. The most common threats include:
Credential theft: Attackers employ tactics such as keylogging, credential stuffing, and
harvesting credentials via malware or insecure endpoints to gain unauthorized access.
Phishing attacks: Social engineering campaigns trick users into revealing login
credentials or approving malicious authentication requests, often bypassing basic
security controls.
Brute force attacks: Automated attempts to guess passwords or authentication tokens
through repeated login attempts, exploiting weak credentials.
Token theft: Cybercriminals may steal authentication tokens from compromised
devices or sessions, enabling them to bypass password requirements and impersonate
legitimate users.
Social engineering: Attackers often use deceptive tactics such as impersonation,
pretexting, or manipulation to trick users into disclosing sensitive information or
performing actions that compromise their identities.
Privilege escalation: Exploiting misconfigured permissions to elevate access rights,
allowing attackers to gain administrative privileges within Entra.
Insider threats: Malicious or negligent actions by users with legitimate access,
including data exfiltration or policy circumvention.
External attacks: Targeted campaigns by advanced persistent threats (APTs),
organized cybercriminals, or state-sponsored actors aiming to compromise Entra for
broader network access.
Misconfiguration Risks: Poorly implemented settings, such as overly permissive
access or idx_4664f8d4 unmonitored legacy authentication, can expose Entra to exploitation.

Zero Trust is predicated on the philosophy of "never trust, always verify." Rather than

demands continuous evaluation of user and device identities, contextual risk, and explicit
policy enforcement for every access request. The foundational principles of Zero Trust include:
Verify Explicitly: Authenticate and authorize every access attempt using all available

Use Least Privilege Access: Limit user and application permissions to only what is
necessary, reducing the attack surface and mitigating potential damage from a
compromise.
Assume Breach: Design security controls and monitoring under the assumption that
attackers may already be present, enabling rapid detection, response, and containment

premises idx_28821021 domain controllers. Most organizations aspire to be in this stage in the long-term. In
this stage, there are no on-premises domain controllers and users, groups and devices are
created and managed directly in Microsoft Entra ID. All applications and services that used to
depend on Active Directory have been modernized.

Chapter 17 584
Migration strategies
There is no idx_b99ca0fc one-size-fits-all approach to migrating from Active Directory to Microsoft Entra ID.
The optimal strategy depends on your organization's size, complexity, legacy dependencies,
risk tolerance, and timeline. The four primary strategies are outlined below.
Phased migration
A phased migration idx_d46b09e3 is the most common and lowest-risk idx_a90da94a approach. It involves migrating
workloads, users, and applications to Microsoft Entra ID incrementally over a planned
timeline, typically spanning months to years depending on organizational complexity.
Key characteristics:
Identity idx_4c80a02f synchronization is established via Microsoft Entra Connect.
Users and groups are migrated in defined waves, often by department, region, or
business unit.
Applications are modernized or migrated to cloud authentication iteratively.
On-premises AD DS remains operational throughout the transition period.
Each phase includes its own pilot, validation, and rollback plan.
This strategy is best for large enterprises with complex AD environments, multiple forests, and
extensive application dependencies.
Hybrid coexistence
Hybrid coexistence idx_6db64e5d is the most widely adopted approach idx_b4671545 and is often the first step toward a full
cloud migration. In this model, on-premises AD DS and Microsoft Entra ID operate side by
side, with identity synchronization maintaining consistency between the two directories.
Key characteristics:
Microsoft idx_50b03c04 Entra Connect or Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync bridges on-premises AD with
Entra ID.
Users maintain a single identity across both environments.
Cloud authentication is configured for cloud resource access.
Legacy applications continue to use on-premises AD for authentication.
Gradual reduction of on-premises dependencies over time.
This strategy is ideal for organizations that must maintain on-premises infrastructure for
specific workloads while progressively adopting cloud services.

Lift-and-Shift migration
A lift-and-shift idx_a929f259 approach moves existing AD DS domain idx_804a07cf controllers into Azure Infrastructure-
as-a-Service (IaaS) virtual machines while simultaneously establishing Entra ID as the primary
identity provider for cloud workloads.
Key characteristics:
AD DS idx_75810a4d domain controllers are deployed as Azure VMs.
Entra ID is used for cloud application authentication.
Microsoft Entra Domain Services may be used for legacy applications requiring NTLM
or Kerberos.
Reduces physical data center footprint without re-architecting applications.
This strategy suits organizations with significant investment in legacy applications that cannot
be immediately modernized but who want to eliminate physical on-premises infrastructure.

Greenfield (Cloud-Native) approach
A greenfield idx_f7446abd approach establishes Microsoft Entra ID as the sole identity idx_1fdaed06 provider from the
start, with no dependency on on-premises Active Directory.
Key characteristics:
No on-premises idx_870a6bbe AD DS infrastructure is deployed or maintained.
All devices are Entra ID joined.
Device management is handled entirely through Microsoft Intune and Autopilot.
All applications use modern authentication protocols like SAML, OIDC, and OAuth.
Group Policy is replaced entirely by Intune configuration profiles and compliance
policies.
This is most viable for new organizations, divisions, or post-merger scenarios where no legacy
AD footprint exists.
Journey to the cloud
Transformation to the cloud is not just the responsibility of the identity team. Organizations
need to idx_60b75fa2 coordinate efforts from all teams, including infrastructure, devices, networks, security,
operations, human resources, and applications, to define policies that include people,
processes, and technology. Support staff must be trained to operate in the new environment.
Effective communication with employees must be planned to ensure that they are aware of any
changes in their way of working. Careful planning must be done before beginning the journey
to ensure a smooth experience for the IT teams and end users.

Prerequisites and planning
Thorough idx_44b74d71 planning is the single most important factor for successful migration. Rushing into
technical implementation without adequate preparation is the most common cause of
migration failures, user disruption, and security gaps.
Organizational readiness
Before idx_e429c489 technical work begins, ensure the following organizational elements are in place:
Executive sponsorship: Secure buy-in from IT leadership and business stakeholders.
Migration affects every user and every application.
Project governance: Establish a cross-functional migration team with representation
from identity, security, networking, application, and end-user support teams.
Communication plan: Develop a comprehensive communication strategy to keep
users informed of changes, timelines, and any actions required on their part.
Change management: Create training materials and support resources, especially for
self-service password reset (SSPR), MFA enrolment, and new sign-in experiences.
Rollback procedures: Document rollback plans for every phase of migration to ensure
rapid recovery in the event of issues.
Once a proper plan has been implemented, it is time to work on the technical details.
Technical prerequisites
The idx_bbf07da2 following technical prerequisites must be satisfied before migration begins.
Verify that all user UPN suffixes match a verified custom domain in Entra ID.
Clean up the on-premises Active Directory by removing stale accounts, standardizing
naming conventions and resolving duplicate or conflicting attributes.
Create emergency break-glass accounts in Entra ID with Global Administrator
privileges, using the *.onmicrosoft.com domain, and exclude them from all
Conditional Access policies.
Deploy Microsoft Entra Connect or Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync on a supported
Windows Server.
Configure Microsoft Entra ID audit logging and diagnostic settings to stream sign-in
and audit logs to a Log Analytics workspace.
Establish a dedicated pilot group of representative users to test each migration phase.
Planning a phased migration from AD to Microsoft Entra ID helps ensure a smooth transition
with minimal downtime.

Identity synchronization
Identity synchronization is the foundational step in most migration strategies. It creates a
bridge idx_65e06435 between on-premises AD and Microsoft Entra ID, ensuring that user identities, group
memberships, and attributes are consistent across both directories. Depending on the
organization's requirements, you can use Microsoft Entra Connect Sync or Microsoft Entra
Cloud Sync. These have been discussed in detail in Chapter 3, Implementing Microsoft Entra ID.
Migrating authentication
Selecting and implementing the correct authentication method is one of the most
consequential idx_c74c3a93 decisions in migration. Microsoft Entra ID supports three primary
authentication methods for hybrid environments, each with distinct characteristics, security
profiles, and infrastructure requirements. These are password hash sync, pass-through
authentication, and federation using AD FS. These have been discussed in detail in Chapter 3,
Implementing Microsoft Entra ID. Review each method carefully before choosing the right
method for your organization, as this decision is difficult to change later.
If your organization is using AD FS, migration to cloud authentication is a key step involving
several dependencies like removing applications that depend on AD authentication. It is
recommended to follow a staged rollout capability that enables selective testing of cloud
authentication methods with specific user groups before performing a full domain cutover.

Migration approaches by application type
Depending idx_e1815f09 on the type of application, different methods of migration will apply. The following
